item.title: Ise Jingu Naiku: Japan's Holiest Shrine — Guide
item.description: Ise Jingu’s Naiku (Inner Shrine) is the most sacred site in all of Shinto, enshrining Amaterasu-Omikami, the sun goddess and mythical ancestor of the imperial line, whose sacred mirror — one of the three imperial regalia — is said to be kept here. Reached across the arched Uji Bridge and up a broad gravel path through towering thousand-year cedars, the shrine is famous for the Shikinen Sengu, the ritual by which its main halls are rebuilt from fresh hinoki cypress on an adjacent site every 20 years — a 1,300-year-old cycle of renewal, most recently in 2013, that keeps this ancient architecture eternally new.

item.title: Ise Jingu Complete Guide: Japan's Most Sacred Shrine
item.description: Ise Jingu stands apart from every other sacred site in Japan. Not by scale — there are shrine complexes that cover more ground — but by the nature of its significance. For over 2,000 years, Ise has been the spiritual centre of the Japanese nation, the home of Amaterasu Omikami, the sun goddess from whom the imperial family traces its divine lineage. The Emperor of Japan makes a personal visit to Ise at the beginning of each reign.
